newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Cigar distributor, finance co jump.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS-Cigar distributor, finance co jump.

text.p: Shares of a cigar distributor 800-JR Cigar Inc and specialty finance company New Century Financial Corp both jumped on Thursday, after both were priced above estimates.

Shares of 800 JR-Cigar jumped 18 percent, adding 3-1/8 to 20-1/8 from their IPO price of 17, which was above the estimated range of $14 to $16. The company, based in Whippany, New Jersey, sold three million shares in the offering.
In its prospectus JR-Cigar said it was the largest U.S. distributor and retailer of premium cigars.
800-JR Cigar, which focuses on the high-end, high-profit premium cigar market, distributes proprietary brands Belinda, Casa Blanca, El Rey del Mundo among others.
The company is also the largest customer for many of the world's leading cigar makers such as Consolidated Cigar Holdings Inc, General Cigar Holdings Inc and Swisher International Inc.
It sells cigars and cigarettes by direct mail and in six specialty cigar stores and two North Carolina discount outlet stores.
The company earned $2.4 million on sales of $152.7 million in 1995, according to the prospectus.
About 25 percent of the company was sold in the equity offering, led by Wheat First Butcher Singer.

New Century Financial jumped more than 20 percent in its first trading, with shares tacking on 2-1/2 to 13-1/2. The company offered 2.9 million of the 3.5 million shares sold, with existing shareholders selling the rest.
The shares were priced by Montgomery Securities at $11, above their estimated range of $8.50 to $10.50 each.

Another company, Staff Leasing Inc also gained, rising 1-1/8 to 18-1/8. It priced at the top of its estimated price talk of $15-$17 per share by lead underwriter Lehman Brothers. Montgomery was a co-underwriter of the offering.

Staff Leasing is a professional employer organization offering payroll, benefits, human resource consulting and other services to small and mid-size companies. It lost $24.9 million in 1995 and $3.9 million in 1996.
